result.summary: This isn't a maintenance job. The landlord reports rent arrears and a dispute over a deposit from a previous tenancy. He also wants the locks changed so the tenant can't get in until he pays, which is likely an unlawful eviction. I did not arrange a contractor. I escalated the case to a human at high priority, emailed the landlord to say the case is with the lettings team and that we won't change the locks, and recorded the facts on the property and tenant records. The ticket stays in intake because it shouldn't go through the repair stages.

judgement.why_this_decision: In event 001 the landlord asks the agency to 'deal with' alleged rent arrears and a deposit from an earlier tenancy, and to 'change the locks so he cannot get in until he pays'. Event 002 shows no repair is needed. Arrears, deposits and possession are not maintenance matters and need agency and legal judgement. Changing the locks to keep out a tenant without a court order is likely unlawful eviction under the Protection from Eviction Act 1977, so following the instruction would cause harm. classify_reply returned 'review' with needs_human_response at 0.95.

alternatives_considered.why_not: Likely unlawful eviction or harassment of a tenant who still lives there. No fault with the locks has been reported.

alternatives_considered.option: Contact the tenant about the arrears
alternatives_considered.why_not: Arrears and deposits are not the maintenance team's job, and contacting him could make the dispute worse. The lettings team should decide how to approach him.
The landlord is waiting for a reply and could change the locks himself. He needed a prompt warning and the case needed a human.
